title.narrative: Humanitarian mine action and protection against explosive weapons in Ukraine

description.narrative:
The project ‘Humanitarian mine action and protection against explosive weapons: Ukraine’ is implemented by the Mines Advisory Group (MAG) in partnership with the Ukrainian Deminers Association (UDA). The project’s main objective is to protect civilians from landmines, cluster munitions and other explosive ordnance through an integrated approach combining non-technical survey, technical survey and clearance, explosive ordnance risk education, victim assistance, and support to national mine action governance and coordination. The project is aligned with Ukraine’s National Mine Action Strategy 2024–2033. The intended target group are civilians affected by explosive ordinance, with priority given to the most vulnerable groups in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv. The project strengthens localisation, national ownership, and the capacity of Ukrainian institutions and implementing organisations, while ensuring that operations are grounded in humanitarian principles, international mine action standards, accountability, conflict sensitivity and gender responsiveness. International Alert (IA) will work alongside MAG and UDA to institutionalise conflict-sensitive and gender-responsive practices, ensuring mine action activities reinforce social cohesion and local ownership.
The expected effects for the target group of the project (outcomes) are Outcome l: Measurable progress towards treaty compliance and universalisation Outcome 2: Responsive and equitable nationally-owned mine action through improved governance and with increased local implementation Outcome 3: Mine action integrated or sequenced with humanitarian, development, peacebuilding or stabilisation initiatives Outcome 4: Safe and productive land use improves livelihoods and basic services, improving quality of life and the environment Outcome 5: Risk of harm reduced increases returns and freedom of movement
